mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has risen in every one of the last four weeks (7.4 to 9.0), indicating a persistent behavioral shift toward staying home. This sustained trend is expected to keep suppressing discretionary retail and recreation visits over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose monotonically from 7.4 to 9.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: If mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is higher than over the last 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL continuing to rise, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility dropped sharply week-on-week from -31.9 to -34.1, a 2.2 point acceleration. If this rate of decline exceeds 2 points in a single week, it signals an abrupt reduction in out-of-home trip-taking that should transmit to lower RETAIL_REC within two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT fell from -31.9 to -34.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks despite the TRANSIT acceleration, the threshold mechanism is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility rising while WORKPLACES mobility simultaneously plateaus or declines indicates a joint hunkering-down pattern where people are neither commuting nor leaving home for errands, compounding to depress RETAIL_REC more than either series would alone.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL rises and WORKPLACES falls or stays flat in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 7.4 to 9.0 while WORKPLACES moved from -29.0 to -30.1
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks even though RESIDENTIAL keeps rising and WORKPLACES stays flat or falls, the interaction hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of tightening restrictions associated with a new variant wave, the combination of falling TRANSIT and erratic PARKS mobility (no sustained recovery) signals policy-driven or precautionary avoidance of public spaces, which should continue to suppress RETAIL_REC over the next month.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS oscillated between -10.6 and -4.7 without a clear recovery trend
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC increases over the next 4 weeks while TRANSIT remains depressed and PARKS stays volatile, the policy-driven suppression mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: With the snapshot taken in mid-December, approaching end-of-year holidays typically drive a short-term seasonal surge in retail visits for gift and holiday shopping, even amid general mobility caution, producing a one-week uptick in RETAIL_REC before reverting.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date is 2021-12-15, within the holiday shopping season
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following the snapshot despite the holiday period, the seasonal surge hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility rebounded from -10.6 to -4.7 in the latest week. If PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-over-week, it signals renewed outdoor and local activity that often coincides with nearby retail and recreation visits within the same week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-over-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS increased from -10.6 to -4.7 in the most recent week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to fall in the week following a PARKS rebound exceeding 5 points, the activity-linkage hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A divergence where WORKPLACES mobility stays roughly stable (-29 to -30) while TRANSIT falls sharply suggests selective, policy-driven avoidance of public transit and shared spaces rather than a broad economic slowdown, which should continue to depress RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks as shoppers avoid transit-dependent trips.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls more than WORKPLACES by at least 3 points in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES stayed near -29 to -30 while TRANSIT fell from -30.4 to -34.1
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rebounds over the next two weeks despite continued TRANSIT decline and stable WORKPLACES, the selective-avoidance hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has become less negative in recent weeks (-4.9 to -2.1), suggesting households are consolidating errands into fewer, essential-only trips. This substitution behavior is expected to divert visits away from broader retail and recreation destinations in the short term.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM improved from -4.9 to -2.1 in the latest week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rises in the week following a GROCERY_PHARM improvement, the substitution hypothesis is rejected.
